newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index boosted by improved demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index boosted by improved demand.

text.p: A marginal improvement in demand boosted the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index on Thursday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index rose 22 points to stand at 3105.56. Turnover was posted at 24.754 million shillings traded on 800,383 shares from 22.941 million shillings traded on 538,393 shares on Wednesday.
Brokers said the index was pushed up by sustained demand on Kenya Commercial Bank, Uchumi Supermarket and Kenya Breweries which pushed prices up.
"Prices fluctuated quite a bit during the trading hours, but by the close most of the key shares were up marginally," a senior broker said.
Kenya Airways which has been trading below 8.0 closed at 8, pushed up by an increase in demand for the shares.

"It looks like the price might just be picking up although it's still too early to tell," another broker said. "You know many people were selling because they panicked when the price started falling," he added.
Turnover was boosted by a single deal on the three-day special offer board where 450,000 shares of East African Portland Cement were traded at 21 from 20.
Brokers said they expected the upward trend in the index seen in the last two weeks to continue because there was enough demand especially from foreigners to sustain it.

"There is a lot demand out there from foreigners who have a lot of confidence in our emerging market, infact we're having a problem because we're not being able to match their orders," one broker said.
Rea Vipingo traded 13,000 shares at 10 from 10.50, while Kenya Oil Company traded at 50 unchanged.
